newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian government wins fresh confidence vote.
newsitem.headline: Italian government wins fresh confidence vote.

text.p: Italy's centre-left government won a confidence vote in the Chamber of Deputies (lower house) on Thursday which it had called to push through a draft law on reforms of the civil service and public administration.
The victory by 315 votes to 185 ensured passage of articles of the bill which had not yet been debated because of what the government argued were opposition delaying tactics.

Prime Minister Romano Prodi relies for his majority in the lower house on the hard left party Communist Refoundation, which almost brought down the government last week by voting against deployment of Italian troops in Albania.
It voted with the government in Thursday's confidence vote.
The draft bill is designed to simplify Italy's stifling public bureaucracy and transfer many of the powers now held by national civil servants to local and regional authorities.

It passed through the Senate (upper house) last July but had been stalled in the lower house by opposition politicians absenting themselves from the chamber and denying a quorum. A vote on the bill itself is scheduled for April 29.
